claims.text: 25.2% of middle and high school students reported using social networking sites for more than 2 hours every day.
Students reporting an unmet need for mental health support are more likely to use social networking sites for more than 2 hours per day than those without unmet needs.
Daily social networking site use of more than 2 hours is independently associated with poor self-rated mental health in children and adolescents.
Daily social networking site use of more than 2 hours is independently associated with high levels of psychological distress in children and adolescents.
Daily social networking site use of more than 2 hours is independently associated with suicidal ideation in children and adolescents.

evidence.description: Overall, 25.2% of students reported using SNSs for more than 2 hours every day.
Students who reported unmet need for mental health support were more likely to report using SNSs for more than 2 hours every day than those with no identified unmet need for mental health support.
Daily SNS use of more than 2 hours was also independently associated with poor self-rating of mental health.
Daily SNS use of more than 2 hours was also independently associated with experiences of high levels of psychological distress.
Daily SNS use of more than 2 hours was also independently associated with suicidal ideation.

methodologies.name: Multinomial logistic regression survey analysis
methodologies.description: Multinomial logistic regression was applied to survey data to evaluate associations between social networking site time and youth mental health indicators.
datasets: 2013 Ontario Student Drug Use and Health Survey
conditions: Sample of 753 students (55% female, mean age 14.1 years) in grades 7-12 in Ottawa, Canada

limitations.text: The relationship between the use of Web-based social networking platforms and mental health problems in children and adolescents is unclear.

future_work.text: Enhance the presence of health service providers on social networking sites to offer mental health support to youth.
